title: Remark
body_md: The presence of the correction term $I$ allows the controller to accommodate arbitrarily large initial tracking errors $y^0 - y_{\text{ref}}(0)$, provided that the initial tracking error is known with sufficient accuracy, in order to allow for a suitable $I^0$ that ensures $\left\| e(0) \right\|_{ } \varphi(0) < 1$.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md: While the bound prescribed by $\varphi$ holds for $e(t) = y(t) - y_{\text{ref}}(t) + I(t)$, we can use the boundedness of $I$ to conclude that the tracking error satisfies $\Vert y(t) - y_{\text{ref}}(t) \Vert < \varphi(t)^{-1} + \tilde M$. Since $\tilde M>0$ is determined through design parameters $M,\alpha, \left\| I^0 \right\|_{ }$, the right hand side can resemble an arbitrary bound $\psi \in W^{1,\infty}(\mathds{R}_{\geq 0}, \mathds{R}_{\geq 0})$ with $\inf_{t \geq 0} \psi(t) > 0$.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md: The choice of $\tilde{M}$ entails a trade-off between the admissable sampling interval lengths and the resulting transient performance bounds. Choosing $\tilde{M} $ such that $\frac{\tilde{M}}{c(\tilde{M})}$ is maximized yields the least restrictive a priori bound on the sampling interval length and hence allows for the coarsest sampling scheme. On the other hand, choosing $\tilde{M}$ small reduces the offset from the prescribed performance bound, since $\Vert I \Vert_{\infty} \leq \tilde{M}$. Thus, when tighter safety margins are desired, $\tilde{M}$ can be decreased, at the expense of a more restrictive bound on the lengths of the sampling intervals.

label: Lem:F
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Corollary
body_md: Consider the closed-loop system~\eqref{eq:System},~\eqref{eq:Controller} with the time-triggered sampling operator $S_T$ replacing $S_M$ in~\eqref{eq:Controller}. Choose $M,h >0$ and assume that~\eqref{eq:condF} holds, so that we can choose $\alpha>0$ small enough with $t_{\min}(\tilde M) \geq h$ by Lemma~\ref{Lem:F}. Let the sampling sequence $(t_k)$ be such that $t_{k+1} - t_k \le h$ for all $k\in\mathds{N}$. Assume that the initial values satisfy $\Vert y^0 - y_{\text{ref}}(0) + I^0 \Vert < 1$ and $\left\| I^0 \right\|_{ } < \tilde{M}$. Then the closed-loop system has a global solution satisfying $\varphi(t) \left\| e(t) \right\|_{ } < \varepsilon$ for all times $t\geq 0$, for some $\varepsilon \in (0,1)$, with $u$ remaining bounded, and $\Vert I \Vert_{\infty} \leq \tilde{M}$.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md: Lemma~\ref{Lem:F} guarantees that, under a suitable growth condition on $F$, the parameters $\alpha,M>0$ can be chosen to accommodate an arbitrarily large bound $t_{\min}(\tilde M)\ge h$ on the sampling intervals for given $h>0$. If this condition is not satisfied, the largest achievable bound may be limited. In either case, an upper bound on $F$, and hence some knowledge of the system dynamics, is required to select suitable parameters $\alpha,M>0$ for a given $h$, in contrast to the event-triggered controller in Theorem~\ref{Thm:event}, which does not require such knowledge.
